nodes.statement: a proof (construction, density argument, or transfer theorem) that divergent reciprocal sum forces unbounded attained AP lengths
verification that the AP predicate used matches the Lean library's Set.IsAPOfLength (no unstated d ≥ 1 or distinctness strengthening unless the library itself imposes it)
explicit handling of the ∃ᶠ quantifier: unboundedness of attained lengths, not merely infinitely many APs of one fixed length

AFFIRMATIVE: prove that for every A ⊆ ℕ with divergent reciprocal sum, the set of k for which A contains some S ⊆ A with S.IsAPOfLength k is unbounded in ℕ (equivalently ∃ᶠ k in atTop, per the Lean statement). This may be done either by a direct proof or by proving a stronger statement (e.g. all k, or positive-density transfer) — a stronger proof is acceptable since it entails the target.
an explicit or existence-proof counterexample set A with divergent reciprocal sum
a proof that A's AP lengths are bounded (no IsAPOfLength-k subset for any k above the bound), matching the negation of Filter.Frequently
consistency of the construction with the library's IsAPOfLength conventions (difference-zero degenerate APs included or excluded exactly as the library decides)

NEGATIVE: construct (or prove existence of) a set A ⊆ ℕ with ∑_{n∈A} 1/n = ∞ whose attained AP lengths are bounded above — i.e. there is some K such that for all k > K, no S ⊆ A has S.IsAPOfLength k. This is the exact negation of ∃ᶠ; it suffices that only finitely many lengths k are attained (e.g. no APs longer than some fixed K0), which is weaker than missing one specific length while possibly containing longer APs.

Erdos problem 3 (erdosproblems.com/3, OPEN). Verbatim source statement: "If $A\subseteq \mathbb{N}$ has $\sum_{n\in A}\frac{1}{n}=\infty$ then must $A$ contain arbitrarily long arithmetic progressions?" Formalized (Lean, verbatim): ∀ A : Set ℕ, (¬ Summable fun a : A ↦ 1 / (a : ℝ)) → ∃ᶠ (k : ℕ) in Filter.atTop, ∃ S ⊆ A, S.IsAPOfLength k. The conclusion is Filter.Frequently at ∃ᶠ: for every N there exists some k ≥ N such that A contains an arithmetic progression of length k — i.e. AP lengths attained by A are unbounded (infinitely many lengths k are realized), NOT that every k is realized.

nodes.definitions:
def apFree3 (s : Finset (Fin 5)) : Prop := ∀ a b c : Fin 5, a ∈ s → b ∈ s → c ∈ s → a < b → b < c → (b.val - a.val) ≠ (c.val - b.val)

def check_r3_5 : Prop := (∀ s : Finset (Fin 5), apFree3 s → s.card ≤ 4) ∧ apFree3 ({0, 1, 3, 4} : Finset (Fin 5)) ∧ ({0, 1, 3, 4} : Finset (Fin 5)).card = 4)
